key_insight: Random sampling maps provide a unified way to compare and compress inputs of different sizes, enabling both size-generalization analysis and efficient sketching for variable-sized data.
engineering_relevance: This gives practical guidance for building models and evaluators that must handle sequences, point clouds, graphs, or tensors whose sizes at test time may exceed training sizes.
method: Define sampling operators that relate larger and smaller instances across sizes.
Match each domain to an appropriate sampling notion based on its symmetries and instance relations.
Derive explicit generalization and sketching rates for function classes continuous under the chosen sampling notion.
evidence_signal: The paper is theoretical and reports explicit rates and domain examples rather than empirical benchmark results.
watch_item: The framework’s usefulness depends on choosing a sampling notion that correctly matches the domain symmetry; a poor choice may weaken the guarantees or make the sketching approximation inaccurate.
